title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 251
paragraphs: The priests of the gods in other lands wear long hair, but in Egypt they shave their heads. Among other men the custom is that in mourning those whom the matter concerns most closely have their hair cut short, but the Egyptians, when deaths occur, let their hair grow long — both that on the head and that on the chin — having before been close shaven. Other men have their daily living separate from beasts, but the Egyptians have theirs together with their beasts. Other men live on wheat and barley, but to any Egyptian who makes his living from these it is a great reproach; they make their bread of emmer wheat, which some call spelt. They knead dough with their feet and clay with their hands, with which they also gather up dung. Whereas other men, except those who have learned otherwise from the Egyptians, leave their private parts as nature made them, the Egyptians practise circumcision. As for garments, the men wear two each and the women only one. Whereas others fasten the rings and ropes of the sails on the outside of the ship, the Egyptians do this on the inside. Finally, in the writing of characters and in reckoning with pebbles, while the Hellenes carry the hand from left to right, the Egyptians do so from right to left; and doing so they say they do it in the right-handed manner and the Hellenes in the left-handed. They use two kinds of characters in writing, one called sacred and the other common.
